title: PTE Speaking: Every Task and How to Score It
summary: Read Aloud, Repeat Sentence, Describe Image, Retell Lecture and the rest — what the AI rewards, task by task.

nodes.label: Read Aloud
nodes.note: Speak the text on screen (speaking + reading)

nodes.label: Repeat Sentence
nodes.note: Hear it, say it back exactly (listening + speaking)

nodes.label: Retell Lecture
nodes.note: Summarise a short lecture in your words

chunks.heading: Fluency and pronunciation are the scores
chunks.body: Across almost every speaking task the AI marks two things: **oral fluency** (a steady, natural flow without long pauses or restarts) and **pronunciation** (clear, intelligible sounds). **Content matters, but a fluent, clear delivery is what separates a good score from an average one.**
chunks.realExample: In Read Aloud, a candidate who reads at a calm, even pace with no stumbles beats one who reads faster but restarts twice — even if both cover every word.
chunks.memoryHook: Flow beats speed. Never restart — a stumble costs less than a stop.

chunks.heading: Read Aloud & Repeat Sentence — the double-scorers
chunks.body: **Read Aloud**: a short text appears; after a short prep, read it aloud (scores **speaking + reading**). **Repeat Sentence**: hear a sentence once and say it back exactly (scores **listening + speaking**). Both are high-value because they feed two skills.
chunks.realExample: Repeat Sentence tip: don't try to 'understand' long sentences — chunk them into 3–4 word groups and echo the rhythm. Getting most words in the right order scores well.
chunks.memoryHook: Read Aloud = speak+read. Repeat Sentence = listen+speak. Two-for-one.

chunks.heading: Describe Image & Retell Lecture — structure saves you
chunks.body: **Describe Image**: describe a graph, map or picture aloud. **Retell Lecture**: listen to a short lecture, then recount it. For both, a **fixed spoken template** keeps you fluent: open → 2–3 key features → a closing line, filling the whole time without pausing.
chunks.realExample: Describe Image opener you can reuse: 'This image shows… The most striking feature is… followed by… Overall, it suggests…' — a scaffold that stops you freezing on an unfamiliar chart.
chunks.memoryHook: Have a reusable opener + closer. Fill the time; silence is the only real fail.

chunks.heading: The short ones and the newer tasks
chunks.body: **Answer Short Question**: reply in one or a few words. PTE has also added tasks like **Summarize Group Discussion** and **Respond to a Situation** — listen to a scenario or discussion, then give a spoken response. Same rule: **keep talking clearly until the time or your point is done.**
chunks.realExample: Answer Short Question: 'What do we call frozen water?' → just say 'ice.' Don't over-explain — these are quick, factual, one-word wins.
chunks.memoryHook: Short question = short answer. Everything else: fill the time, stay clear.

recall.q: What two things does the AI score across most PTE speaking tasks?
recall.a: Oral fluency (steady, natural flow) and pronunciation (clear, intelligible speech).

recall.q: Which two skills does Read Aloud contribute to?
What is the best strategy if you can't remember a full sentence in Repeat Sentence?
recall.a: Chunk it into 3–4 word groups and echo the rhythm — getting most words in order still scores.

recall.q: Why use a fixed template for Describe Image and Retell Lecture?
recall.a: It keeps you fluent and fills the time without pausing, which protects your fluency score.

recall.q: What should you avoid at all costs in the speaking tasks?
recall.a: Long pauses and restarts — silence and stopping hurt the fluency score most.
